method: 人工编辑映射：每张卡把一组已收录的财报问答（analysts/corpus.json）按主题连接到 Hot Chips 2017–2026 观众提问模式（hot-chips 年度页）、架构师追问、人物与笔记。Hot Chips 一侧引用各年度页面的“Patterns in the reviewed Q&A”原文摘要及录像时间点；主题占比取自 heatmap-data.csv，各年来源口径不同（2026 为 Slack 与现场问答汇总，分母更大），仅用于看趋势方向。架构追问与 Hot Chips 式提问是待检验的问题，不是已核实结论；本页不包含未经来源核实的数字。

skill_map.why: 供需约束要追到瓶颈资源与完整服务成本。
CapEx 传导取决于规模扩展与哪一环节先受限。
单位经济要落到 PPA、TCO 与产品是否值得交付。
盈利质量要拆开量、价与成本，并回到真实负载。
指引解码要区分承诺、产能与实际可交付。
增长二阶变化对应投入与产出之间的时滞和瓶颈迁移。
证伪论点要挑战假设，并找出能反驳的生产证据。

architect_followups: HBM3E→HBM4 的堆叠层数、裸片面积、基底裸片与封装步骤各改变了单位 bit 消耗的晶圆等价量吗？需要哪份公开来源来核实？

cards.boundary: 这些追问用于建模，不替代厂商披露；任何晶圆等价比例都必须有来源，否则只能写成假设。

patterns.title: Memory needs lifecycle accounting.
patterns.summary: Mythic's intermediate activations occupied tile SRAM; A64FX had an HBM capacity ceiling. Optane answers withheld requested endurance and operating-state power figures. Density and bandwidth alone did not establish service lifetime or working-set fit.

patterns.title: Memory choice follows workload and economics.
patterns.summary: Pensando justified HBM-to-DDR migration through capacity flexibility, buffering and cost. Tenstorrent distinguished inference LPDDR4 from training GDDR6. Xbox balanced GPU bandwidth with CPU latency. No single memory hierarchy won every workload.

patterns.title: Feed the accelerator before judging arithmetic.
patterns.summary: Samsung attributed the gap between PIM bandwidth uplift and application speedup to unchanged host and ordering overheads. Facebook emphasized ingestion benchmarking and reuse. Translation, DRAM-bank behavior and preprocessing still limited useful throughput.

patterns.title: Memory placement and coherence drew sustained probing.
patterns.summary: AMD confirmed directed probes but left protocol details unresolved. Questions also tested HBM access efficiency, PIM interfaces and memory overhead.

patterns.title: Packaging needs economic and test evidence.
patterns.summary: EMIB questions probed access, cost and known-good-die assurance. EPYC's organic package prompted performance and die-yield questions. Integration feasibility did not settle supplier access, usable yield or the complete platform tradeoff.

patterns.title: Integration adds power, test and trust gates.
patterns.summary: Lakefield described known-good-die testing but left stacking limits unquantified. Tesla's dual-SoC safety intent did not specify disagreement handling. Jintide's monitor answer did not establish a complete host trust boundary.

patterns.title: Packaging raised integration questions.
patterns.summary: Chiplet arrangement, verification, materials and assembly all drew scrutiny. Physical integration answers were more concrete than future interoperability plans.

patterns.title: Optics exposed packaging and repair tradeoffs.
patterns.summary: Thermal paths, fiber connections and driver placement drew scrutiny. External laser replacement left internal optical-engine repair unresolved.

patterns.title: Density and power need separate proof.
patterns.summary: Intel discussed PowerVia with stacking and EMIB's yield/reach tradeoffs. Anton justified a global clock mesh through latency and power. TSMC cooling questions lacked useful caption answers; package scalability did not establish facility feasibility.

patterns.title: Cooling scrutiny included operational maturity.
patterns.summary: Google described favorable operating experience. Fabric8 Labs said lifetime testing remained outstanding, despite promising thermal results.

patterns.title: Cooling was examined at system level.
patterns.summary: Questions covered rack limits, maintenance, capex and prototype evidence. Chip heat removal alone did not settle the facility decision.

patterns.title: Interconnect names leave mechanisms unresolved.
patterns.summary: Arm's cache stashing needed software and interface prerequisites; Xilinx qualified its nonblocking-mesh claim through traffic-class isolation. AWS discussed placement groups and packet-aware limiting. Topology and peak link rate did not describe congestion behavior.

patterns.title: Useful scale includes failed links.
patterns.summary: Tofino telemetry distinguished local timing from WAN synchronization. Fungible emphasized connectivity; TPU Pod recovery details remained incomplete. Cerebras described redundant cores and routes. Nominal line rate did not establish degraded-mode behavior.

patterns.title: Fabric mechanisms mattered beyond bandwidth.
patterns.summary: Questions probed retries, buffers, programmable controls and mixed-vendor operation. Interoperability did not establish equal performance.

patterns.title: Fabric behavior.
patterns.summary: Routing, shared bandwidth and recovery mattered alongside aggregate link rates.

patterns.title: Formats and software constrain specialization.
patterns.summary: Brainwave questions pressed precision and accuracy assumptions. TPU exchanges examined workload size, sparsity and framework selection. AWS F1 required manual partitioning across FPGAs. Hardware specialization still demanded model and application work.

patterns.title: Programmability shifts work into mapping.
patterns.summary: Project Everest disclosed no autovectorizing compiler and deferred receive-programming details. Pixel Visual Core and dynamic-graph questions tested what developers still had to map and synchronize. Higher-level access did not prove transparent application portability.

patterns.title: Software readiness changes the value of hardware
patterns.summary: NVIDIA described Transformer Engine as hardware plus software; AMD described framework integration as ongoing. Intel separated demonstrated throughput from a newer specification calculation, and Biren distinguished standard benchmark settings from customer-specific models. Evaluation needs the exact software release, workload and measurement basis.

patterns.title: Software compatibility is part of the architecture.
patterns.summary: ROCm coverage, vector support and compiler responsibility drew questions across vendors. A hardware feature did not establish a usable software path.

patterns.title: Software control.
patterns.summary: Framework support did not settle porting effort or placement control.

patterns.title: Efficiency claims need matching boundaries.
patterns.summary: Samsung's power comparison was not fully process-normalized. XDNN described mapped compute rather than all FPGA resources. NRAM cell energy and Mythic whole-chip energy covered different budgets; their ratios could not be compared directly.

patterns.title: Peak compute needs workload evidence.
patterns.summary: Huawei and Spring Crest faced benchmark and MLPerf questions. Cerebras deferred working-system performance. Microsoft's compression comparison used different algorithms. Those answers exposed comparison boundaries that peak throughput alone could not resolve.

patterns.title: Benchmarks need full pipeline boundaries.
patterns.summary: DeepMind treated MLPerf as useful but insufficient for evolving research. Lightmatter separated simulator results and analog timing from measured digital performance. Conversion, transfers, host work and workload diversity remained essential comparison terms.

patterns.title: Metric boundaries changed the interpretation.
patterns.summary: Marvell excluded DRAM latency from its expander figure. dMatrix reported a core efficiency metric; NVIDIA clarified the traffic used in its noise test.

patterns.title: Comparable performance.
patterns.summary: Participants challenged precision, workloads and measurement boundaries, not just headline speedups.
